Direct 2024 evidence on nuclear command-and-control is structurally thin because Mexico is not a nuclear-armed state, so the best available evidence is from civilian nuclear safety, radiological regulation, emergency preparedness, and spent-fuel custody at Laguna Verde. I did not find a Mexico-specific 2024 public record about nuclear-weapon command-and-control, because Mexico has no nuclear arsenal. So the evidence is necessarily indirect and centered on civilian nuclear safety, radiological regulation, emergency planning, and spent-fuel custody.","evidence":[{"title":"Entrada en vigor de la NOM-008-NUCL-2024","publisher":"Comisión Nacional de Seguridad Nuclear y Salvaguardias / Gobierno de México","date":"2024-06-20","url":"https://www.gob.mx/cnsns/articulos/entrada-en-vigor-de-la-nom-008-nucl-2024?idiom=es","summary":"Mexico updated radiological contamination limits and criteria for control, explicitly to minimize exposure and tighten controls at radiological and nuclear installations.
